docs.title: Cue Documentation
docs.text:
Cue is a distributed, in-memory job queue with Raft-based consistency, automatic retries, and dead letter handling.

It is designed for teams that need reliable job dispatch without operating complex infrastructure like Kafka.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
• Cue — The distributed cluster (3/5/7 nodes)
  • CueProxy — Stateless HTTP & WebSocket gateway

docs.title: Quick Links
docs.text:
• Cue Quick Start
  • CueProxy Quick Start
  • Cue GitHub
  • CueProxy GitHub

Cue is not a Kafka replacement. It is a bounded, simple, and operationally light job queue.

docs.title: Administrative Operations
docs.text:
Promote Learner 

curl -X POST http://localhost:8321/cluster/promote-learner \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -d '{"node_id": "node4"}'

Demote Voter / Remove Node 

curl -X POST http://localhost:8321/cluster/demote-voter \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -d '{"node_id": "node2"}'

Transfer Leadership 

curl -X POST http://localhost:8321/cluster/transfer-leader \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -d '{"target_node_id": "node3"}'

All admin endpoints require a token with admin role.

docs.title: Full Configuration Reference
docs.text:
node_id: "node1"
data_dir: "./data/node1"

cluster:
  listen_addr: "0.0.0.0"
  quic_port: 8323
  cert_path: "./certs/node1.pem"
  key_path: "./certs/node1_key.pem"
  ca_path: "./certs/ca_cert.pem"
  initial_voters: ["node1", "node2", "node3"]
  peers: ["node1", "node2", "node3"]

proxy:
  addr: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8322
  cert_path: "./certs/node1.pem"
  key_path: "./certs/node1_key.pem"
  ca_path: "./certs/ca_cert.pem"

api:
  listen_addr: "0.0.0.0"
  api_port: 8321
  token_path: "./configs/auth.yml"

partition:
  active_queue_capacity: 1000000
  retry_base_delay_ms: 1000
  max_retries: 3
  max_backoff_ms: 60000

wal:
  compact_after_bytes: 104857600

See the Cue README for all available options and address resolver types. ```

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• In-memory only — Jobs live in RAM (bounded by available memory)
  • No historical replay — Acknowledged jobs are removed
  • Leader-dependent writes — All submissions go through the current leader
  • Bounded capacity — Configurable per-topic queue size
  • Not a streaming platform — Use Kafka for large-scale persistent logs

Cue is ideal for reliable job dispatch with retries, not for event streaming or long-term storage.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Cue exposes Prometheus metrics at /metrics.

docs.title: Important Metrics
docs.text:
• cue_active_queue_depth{topic="..."}
  • cue_jobs_added_total{topic="..."}
  • cue_jobs_completed_total
  • cue_jobs_retried_total
  • cue_jobs_dead_letter_total
  • cluster_leader_changed_total

docs.title: Cue Overview
docs.text: Cue is a distributed, in-memory job queue with strong consistency via Raft.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Producers] --> B[CueProxy]
    C[Consumers] --> B
    B <--> D[Cue Cluster - Leader]
    D <--> E[Follower 1]
    D <--> F[Follower 2]
    style D fill:#4CAF50,stroke:#333

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text:
• Every node holds all partitions (topics) in memory
  • Raft ensures linearizable consistency across the cluster
  • Write-Ahead Log (WAL) for durability
  • Automatic retries with exponential backoff
  • Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for failed jobs

CueProxy acts as the stateless gateway for external communication.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Generate TLS certificates for the cluster
  2. Create a configuration file for each node
  3. Start at least 3 nodes
  4. Verify the cluster is healthy

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
./cue serve -config config-node1.yml

Full configuration examples and multi-node startup scripts are available in the Cue repository. ```

docs.title: Producer API
docs.text:
Create Topic 

POST /producer/topic
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{ "topic": "email-notifications" }

Submit Job 

POST /producer/job
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "job": {
    "id": "job-123",
    "topic": "email-notifications",
    "data": "base64-encoded-payload"
  }
}

docs.title: Consumer WebSocket API
docs.text:
Connect to ws://localhost:8080/ws?token=<consumer_token>

See full message reference in the CueProxy README.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Tokens are defined in auth.yml:

tokens:
  - token: prod_token_123
    role: producer
  - token: cons_token_456
    role: consumer
  - token: admin_token_789
    role: admin

Roles: producer, consumer, admin, monitoring.

Tokens are automatically reloaded every 30 seconds.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
api:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8080
  default_max_inflights: 10

cluster:
  cluster_seeds:
    - cue-node-1:8322
    - cue-node-2:8322

auth:
  file: "config/auth.yml"

tls:
  cert_path: "certs/cert.pem"
  key_path: "certs/key.pem"

Full options are available in the CueProxy README.

docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:

docs.title: CueProxy Overview
docs.text: CueProxy is the stateless HTTP and WebSocket gateway for Cue.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Producers] --> B[CueProxy Instances]
    C[Consumers] --> B
    B <--> D[Cue Cluster Leader]
    style B fill:#2196F3
  • Completely stateless & horizontally scalable
  • Handles authentication, load balancing, and backpressure
  • Proxies communicate with Cue via QUIC

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Start a Cue cluster first
  2. Create config.yml
  3. Create auth.yml
  4. Run CueProxy
./cueproxy -config config.yml

Then test:

curl http://localhost:8080/health
